field.name: body
field.p: Resource Planning is a single screen for staffing decisions across several projects at once: which projects are burning hours too fast, who's overloaded this week, and what's still left to hand out on a job you've already charged the client for.
Open it from the app switcher, or Resource Planning → Weekly Plan in the menu.
field.h2: The left column — your project list
field.p: Every active project shows up here (except internal/admin projects and templates, which are hidden on purpose).

ul.li: Search by project name or client at the top.
Filter chips — All, or Left to assign (only projects where you've charged more hours than you've actually handed out to anyone yet — the ones that still need staffing).
Sort by — Health (worst first), Deadline (soonest), or Project name.
Each row shows Due (deadline and days left), Charged (the budget), Allocated (hours actually given to someone), and Unscheduled (given to someone but not yet placed on a specific week).

field.p: Click a project row to pin it to the workspace on the right. Click it again (or the ✕ on its card) to unpin. You can pin as many as you like at once.
field.h2: The right column — your planning workspace
field.p: Each pinned project shows as a card with two header rows:

ul.li: Row 1 — the full project name. Click anywhere on the header to collapse/expand the whole card.

Row 2 — client and dates, "Collapse all tasks" / "Expand all tasks" buttons, the same four stats as the left pane (Charged / Allocated / Left to assign / Unscheduled), a health badge, and the unpin button.

field.p: Below that is the weekly grid: one row per task, and under each task, one row per person assigned to it.

ul.li: The small box next to a person's name is their total hours on that task — how much they've been given overall, regardless of which week.
Each week's column is where you place when those hours actually happen. Type a number, press Tab or click away, and it saves — hours round to the nearest quarter (0.25).
Clear a week's box back to blank to remove that week's plan for that person entirely.
A grey ✕ means that week falls outside the project's own start/deadline dates.
A grey, non-editable cell showing an hour value is a past week — it's showing what was actually logged in Timesheets, not the plan, and can't be edited here. History stays history.

field.p: Adding someone to a task: click "+ Add team member" under that task. Use the role chips on the left of the picker to narrow the list (multi-select — pick several roles at once, or click "All" to clear the selection), then click a person to add them at 0 hours and start filling in their plan.

Top-right of the screen: step back/forward a batch of weeks with the arrows, or jump straight back to the current week with Today. This only changes what's visible — it never moves anyone's actual planned hours.
field.h2: Weekly load strip (bottom of the screen)
field.p: This shows, per person, their total hours across every project they're on — not just the ones you've pinned — for each visible week. It's how you catch someone being overbooked before it happens.

ul.li: Green — within their planning buffer. Amber — past the buffer but still under full capacity. Red — over full capacity.
Search by name, or filter by role (also multi-select — click several roles, or "All" to reset).
The 📌 pin icon next to a name (here or in the planning grid above) adds them to a short list and hides everyone else in this strip — handy once you only care about two or three people.
Hover any cell for the exact numbers behind the color.

field.p: A person's buffer and hard-capacity targets are set on their own record: Employees app → open the person → the "Resource Planning" section, just above the tabs. Buffer defaults to 28h/week, hard capacity to 40h/week, and both can be changed per person.
field.h2: Project health (On track / Stalled / Over burn)
field.p: Shown as a badge on each pinned project's header. It compares how much of the project's timeline has passed against how many hours have actually been logged in Timesheets so far:

ul.li: Over burn — hours are being logged much faster than time is passing. At this rate the charged budget may run out before the deadline.
Stalled — time is passing much faster than hours are being logged. Work may be blocked.
On track — everything else, including any project that's missing a start date or deadline (there's nothing to compare against yet, so it can't flag a problem).

field.p: The "role" used for filtering (CAD Drafter, Structural Engineer, etc.) is each person's Job Position, set on their employee record. Anyone without one assigned shows up as "Team Member" until it's set.
